question: A dealer purchased a water cooler for ₹56,000. He allows a discount of 81% on its marked price and still gains 71%. Find the marked price of the water cooler.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation between **Marked Price (MP)** and **Cost Price (CP)**: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Gain%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

MP ÷ 56000 = (100 + 71) ÷ (100 − 81) = 171 ÷ 19.

MP ÷ 56000 = 9 ÷ 1.

MP = 56000 × 9 = 504000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,04,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP = ₹56,000**, **Gain% = 71%**, **Discount% = 81%**.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f96c7234ea52da0496ed646986f895e22387b8524a1fddf263932efc68a28cdb.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 56000 × (100 + 71) ÷ 100 = 560 × 171 = ₹95,760.
⇒ Let **Marked Price** be MP. SP = MP × (100 − 81) ÷ 100.
⇒ 95760 = MP × 19 ÷ 100.
⇒ MP = (95760 × 100) ÷ 19 = 5040 × 100 = ₹5,04,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,04,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (List Price)**. MP − Discount = SP.

MP-CP Ratio Formula

The most efficient way to solve problems involving both discount and profit is **MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 − D%)**.
